title: What is Zcash (ZEC)? How shielded transactions work

content: Zcash (ZEC) is a privacy-focused cryptocurrency and blockchain launched in 2016. It supports both public and private transactions. Private transactions, known as shielded transactions, utilize zero-knowledge proofs called zk-SNARKs. This technology allows the network to verify payments securely while keeping the sender, recipient, and transaction amount completely hidden from public view.

'ஷீல்டெட் பரிவர்த்தனைகள்' என்று அழைக்கப்படும் தனிப்பட்ட பரிவர்த்தனைகள், zk-SNARKs எனப்படும் ஜீரோ-நெட்லெட் ஆதாரங்களைப் பயன்படுத்துகின்றன. இந்த தொழில்நுட்பம் அனுப்புநர், பெறுநர் அல்லது தொகையை வெளிப்படுத்தாமல் பாதுகாப்பாகப் பணம் செலுத்துவதைச் சரிபார்க்கிறது.

content_ta: FXStreet தனது YouTube சேனலில் இரண்டு மாதங்களுக்கும் குறைவான காலத்தில் ஒரு மில்லியன் பார்வைகளைக் கடந்து ஒரு முக்கிய மைல்கல்லை எட்டியுள்ளது. இந்த ஈர்க்கக்கூடிய வளர்ச்சி கடந்த ஆண்டைக் காட்டிலும் 1,500 சதவீதத்திற்கும் அதிகமான ஆண்டுக்கு ஆண்டு அதிகரிப்பைக் குறிக்கிறது. ஸ்பெயினின் Barcelona-வைத் தலைமையிடமாகக் கொண்ட இந்நிறுவனத்தின் வீடியோ உள்ளடக்க உத்தியின் வெற்றியையும், அதன் டிஜிட்டல் வளர்ச்சிக்கான முயற்சிகளையும் இந்த சாதனை எடுத்துக்காட்டுகிறது.

title: Two rival Ethereum proposals aim to stop Glamsterdam breaking old contracts
summary: The proposals aim to keep Ethereum’s planned gas changes from breaking existing contracts, using different approaches to what contracts see and what users pay.
content: Two rival Ethereum proposals have been introduced to address potential issues arising from the upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade. The planned gas changes risk breaking existing smart contracts. The new proposals offer different approaches regarding what contracts observe and what users are required to pay, aiming to ensure a seamless transition without disrupting legacy agreements.
content_ta: வரவிருக்கும் Glamsterdam மேம்படுத்தலின் போது ஏற்படக்கூடிய சிக்கல்களைத் தவிர்க்க இரண்டு புதிய Ethereum முன்மொழிவுகள் அறிமுகப்படுத்தப்பட்டுள்ளன. திட்டமிடப்பட்ட எரிவாயு (gas) மாற்றங்கள் ஏற்கனவே உள்ள ஒப்பந்தங்களைச் சிதைக்கக்கூடும் என்பதால், ஒப்பந்தங்கள் எதைப் பார்க்கின்றன மற்றும் பயனர்கள் எதைச் செலுத்த வேண்டும் என்பதில் வெவ்வேறு அணுகுமுறைகளை இந்த முன்மொழிவுகள் வழங்குகின்றன.

title: Bitcoin drops, then pops as Nvidia cheating scandal and failed Iran talks trigger volatility
summary: Volatile price action has once again liquidated leveraged bullish plays worth millions.
content: Bitcoin experienced significant price volatility, dropping and then rebounding. The turbulent market movement was triggered by a combination of geopolitical tensions surrounding failed Iran talks and an unfolding cheating scandal involving Nvidia. This unexpected market action resulted in the liquidation of millions of dollars worth of leveraged bullish positions.
content_ta: Bitcoin விலையில் திடீர் சரிவு மற்றும் மீள் எழுச்சியுடன் கூடிய பெரும் ஏற்றத்தாழ்வு ஏற்பட்டது. Iran பேச்சுவார்த்தைகள் தோல்வியடைந்ததால் ஏற்பட்ட புவிசார் அரசியல் அழுத்தங்கள் மற்றும் Nvidia தொடர்பான முறைகேடு சர்ச்சை ஆகியவை சந்தையில் இந்த நிலைக்கு காரணமாகின. இந்த திடீர் விலை மாற்றத்தால் பல மில்லியன் மதிப்பிலான லாப நோக்கிலான வர்த்தகங்கள் பாதிக்கப்பட்டன.

title: tBTC bridge partially resumes as $120M Aave reserve remains frozen
summary: Threshold halted its tBTC bridge on Oct. 30 as operators addressed a critical Linux kernel vulnerability that could allow attackers to execute code on unpatched servers.
content: Threshold has partially resumed its tBTC bridge following a suspension on October 30. The temporary halt was implemented to allow operators to address a critical Linux kernel vulnerability that posed potential risks of remote code execution on unpatched servers. Meanwhile, a $120M reserve associated with Aave remains frozen as the network continues to work through the security measures.
content_ta: Threshold தனது tBTC பிரிட்ஜ் சேவையை அக்டோபர் 30-ம் தேதிக்குப் பிறகு பகுதியாக மீண்டும் தொடங்கியுள்ளது. பேட்ச் செய்யப்படாத சர்வர்களில் தாக்குதல் நடத்துநர்கள் குறியீட்டை இயக்க வழிவகுக்கும் ஒரு முக்கியமான Linux கர்னல் பாதிப்பை ஆபரேட்டர்கள் சரிசெய்வதற்காக இந்த தற்காலிக நிறுத்தம் செயல்படுத்தப்பட்டது. இதற்கிடையில், Aave தொடர்பான $120M ரிசர்வ் இன்னும் உறைந்த நிலையிலேயே உள்ளது.

title: BVNK Opens OUSD Minting and Payments Across Four Blockchains
summary: BVNK says eligible business customers can now mint, redeem, hold and transfer Open USD (OUSD) on Ethereum, Solana, Base and Tempo. The November 6 rollout…
content: BVNK has launched Open USD (OUSD) minting and payment services for eligible business customers. title: Vitalik Buterin Wants AI to Slow Down, Backs Anti-Data Center Movement

content: Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has expressed support for the anti-data center movement, arguing that slower growth in AI computing power can help buy valuable time. AI கம்ப்யூட்டிங் வளர்ச்சியைக் குறைப்பது மதிப்புமிக்க நேரத்தைப் பெற உதவும் என்றும், எதிர்கால சைபர் பாதுகாப்பு ஆபத்துகளிலிருந்து உலகைப் பாதுகாக்க இந்த எச்சரிக்கையான அணுகுமுறை உதவும் என்றும் அவர் வாதிட்டுள்ளார்.

title: Vitalik Buterin Says ETH Fee Burn Will Not Drive Ethereum's Value
summary:
Vitalik Buterin says the ETH fee burn never was as strong as it seemed and argues ETH should focus on being a store of value instead.

content: Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin recently stated that the ETH fee burn mechanism will not single-handedly drive the value of Ethereum. Instead, Buterin argued that Ethereum should focus on establishing itself as a reliable store of value rather than relying heavily on transaction fee burning mechanics to boost its long-term market price.

title: Nutanix Expands Elevate Partner Program to Include System Integrators and Unlock New Revenue Opportunities for Partners
summary:
Nutanix (NASDAQ: NTNX), a hybrid cloud leader and AI platform company , today announced a significant expansion of its FY27 Elevate Partner Program, representing its largest investment in the program to date. The updates bring systems integrators into Elevate, add incentives for referrals, renewals, and customer expansion, and increase support for partner-led services, giving partners more opportunities to generate revenue beyond the initial technology sale.
The expanded program also supports partners looking to grow their businesses around emerging customer requirements, including enterprise AI, cloud-native applications, and databases. Additional incentives are designed to encourage opportunities involving Nutanix Enterprise AI, Nutanix Database Service (NDB), and Nutanix Kubernetes Platform (NKP), alongside the development of services around these technologies.
The inclusion of systems integrators (SIs) in the program recognises their growing role in shaping IT strategy, designing and integrating solutions, managing migrations, and delivering services. Eligible SIs and consulting partners will also be able to earn referral rewards for identifying and developing Nutanix opportunities, even when they are not the partner responsible for the final sale.
The program creates opportunities for eligible partners across seven areas:
Land: Earn rebates on qualifying net-new Nutanix customer transactions.
Expand: Earn applicable rebates by introducing additional Nutanix solutions into existing customer environments, including enterprise AI, cloud-native technologies, and databases.
Grow: Access benefits that recognise qualifying year-over-year business growth.
Reward: Provide incentives to eligible partner sales and technical employees who help identify or secure qualifying new and expansion opportunities.
Retain: Earn incentives for qualifying on-time renewals.
Refer: Earn referral rewards for qualifying opportunities introduced by eligible systems integrators and consulting partners.
Differentiate: Build verified services capabilities through Powered by Nutanix: Verified Services, with eligible partners able to access Earned Business Development Funds for qualifying go-to-market activities.
Incentives, rebates, referral rewards, and business development funding are subject to applicable program requirements, eligibility criteria, and regional availability.
Nutanix is also expanding support for partner-led services through Powered by Nutanix: Verified Services, helping eligible partners build recognised capabilities in areas such as migrations, deployment, and ongoing customer support. Partners will also have access to standardised Service Delivery Kits and opportunities to shadow Nutanix experts, helping them build the technical expertise and delivery capabilities needed to expand their professional services businesses.
"A partner can spend months helping a customer work out what technology they need, plan a migration or prepare for AI, but they don't always get paid for the work that goes into making a sale happen," said Sven Schoenaerts, Vice President, EMEA Channel and Technology Alliances, Nutanix, "We want to change that. Partners should be able to earn money for bringing us new business, helping existing customers do more with Nutanix and providing the services those customers need. That's especially important for systems integrators and consultants, who often do much of the work before a customer is ready to buy."
Nutanix Cloud Platform's flexibility supports expanded partner opportunities, especially as customers contend with hardware availability, infrastructure costs, and the disruption of major technology upgrades. Support for selected external-storage configurations, including applicable Dell, Everpure, and NetApp technologies, gives partners more options to modernise customer environments while retaining existing infrastructure investments. Nutanix Cloud Clusters (NC2) allows partners to help customers run and move supported workloads between on-premises environments and supported public clouds, providing an alternative when hardware availability or capacity becomes a constraint.
Nutanix is also investing in AI-powered tools to simplify partner engagement and identify new opportunities. Deal Coach, planned for introduction through Nutanix Partner Central later this fiscal year, is designed to support sales-cycle activities. Further planned capabilities include approved visibility into selected customer-environment health, adoption, and lifecycle signals, subject to customer authorisation, helping partners better support customers and plan renewals.

Vivox AI, a provider of explainable AI agents for financial crime compliance, and beSirius, which develops AI for assurance and certification readiness in metals and minerals, today announced a partnership. The companies will bring supplier evidence assessments alongside financial crime checks, helping industrial businesses reduce the time and cost of reviewing suppliers and counterparties.
Mining companies, traders and manufacturers routinely ask suppliers for evidence about their operations. Compliance teams also need to understand who owns those suppliers and whether they are exposed to sanctions or other financial crime risks. These reviews often happen separately. The same information gets requested again, while staff spend time searching through records and following up on unanswered questions.
beSirius AI assesses existing operational and supplier evidence against industry standards and company requirements, identifying gaps and producing source-linked assessments. It supports certification readiness, supplier assessments and continuous assurance, helping companies track corrective actions and address critical risks across operations. Reusing evidence across assessments reduces manual work, saving time and money.
Vivox AI brings specialist financial crime screening to supplier and counterparty reviews. Its explainable AI agents examine sanctions alerts and adverse media, investigate complex ownership structures and help identify the people who ultimately control a business. They draw on corporate records and other sources, keeping an audit trail of the information behind each finding. Vivox AI also helps compliance teams work through potential false positives, cutting time spent on manual research and alert reviews.
The partnership is designed to let teams consider these findings together when reviewing a supplier. beSirius shows which claims have supporting documents and what still needs checking. Vivox AI shows whether the supplier's ownership or screening results call for further investigation. The responsible teams review both before making a decision.
The partnership is relevant to companies across the metals and minerals value chain, from mining and refining to trading and manufacturing. beSirius works with Fortune 500 companies in these sectors.
“The beSirius and Vivox AI integration has strengthened our responsible minerals and metals sourcing efforts, enabling us to reduce the time and manual effort required to gather and assess relevant information, including sustainability policies and management systems, ownership information, sanctions screening, and allegations. By bringing this information together in one place, the integration provides us a more efficient tool to support informed sourcing decisions,” said the sustainability team at a Fortune 500 company.
“Investigating a company's ownership can take considerable time, especially when several entities and jurisdictions are involved,” said Tim Khamzin, founder and CEO of Vivox AI. “Our agents help compliance teams work through that information and check the sources behind the findings. Working with beSirius means those checks can be considered alongside the evidence companies already review when assessing suppliers.”
“Companies often have the documents they need, but finding them and checking them against another set of requirements takes time and money,” said Sergey Tyan, founder and chief commercial officer of beSirius. “beSirius uses that existing evidence to prepare assessments that teams can review. Vivox AI brings financial crime expertise to the same supplier questions, including ownership and sanctions risk.”
For Vivox AI, the partnership brings its experience in financial crime checks for regulated businesses into industrial supply chains. beSirius contributes its work with assurance requirements and evidence across the metals and minerals sector. Their findings address different parts of a supplier review.
The aim is to make those reviews less costly and time-consuming. Companies can reuse evidence rather than collecting the same documents repeatedly, while Vivox AI handles parts of the screening research that would otherwise be done manually. Procurement and compliance teams still review the findings and decide which questions need follow-up.

content: Vivox AI and beSirius have announced a partnership to combine supplier assurance with financial crime compliance for the metals and mining supply chains. The collaboration integrates beSirius's AI-driven operational and supplier evidence assessments with Vivox AI's specialist financial crime screening, sanctions alerts, and ownership structure investigations. This joint approach aims to help industrial businesses significantly reduce manual work, time, and costs associated with reviewing suppliers and counterparties.

title: Solana set for its first tokenized stock venue under SEC framework, listing Galaxy
summary: Formation Securities plans to launch in early 2027 with Galaxy, Exodus and Forward Industries shares, expanding the U.S. regulator's experiment in blockchain-based stock trading.
content: Formation Securities plans to launch the first tokenized stock venue on the Solana blockchain under a U.S. SEC framework. Set for early 2027, the platform will initially list shares of Galaxy, Exodus, and Forward Industries. This development marks a significant expansion of regulatory experiments in blockchain-based stock trading within the United States.

title: Ethereum (ETH) Gas Estimates Are Broken: Explaining the Fix and the Issue
summary: A proposed Geth fix targets Ethereum gas estimates that look correct even when the intended action fails.
content: A proposed fix for Ethereum's Geth client addresses a persistent issue with faulty gas estimates. title: Financial Institutions Accelerate Transition to Multi-Agent AI in Drive for Bottom-Line Value
summary:
Financial institutions are moving beyond isolated agentic AI experiments to multi-agent AI across core banking and insurance workflows. The Capgemini Research Institute’s World Cloud Report for Financial Services 2027 reveals that while 59% of firms are piloting or deploying multi-agent AI in production, only one in ten have achieved the full orchestration required to run them autonomously across the enterprise. To scale successfully, banks and insurers recognize that modernizing their underlying tech stack is a prerequisite to succeed in the agentic AI era – with eight in ten executives prioritizing the reduction of tech debt as a key objective.  
Banks and insurers look to prioritize business outcomes over agentic AI efficiencies
As finance organizations move past individual AI agents to multi-agent systems, the pressure to prove value is intensifying. By 2028, the number of executives prioritizing outcomes as their primary AI-funding criterion is projected to increase 141%, while the number focused on efficiency will drop 42% over the same period, according to the global survey of 1,100 C-suite executives of financial services firms.  
This change in approach comes as financial firms look to balance the capabilities of agentic AI with the cost of deployment.  According to the research,  roughly half of financial services firms cannot consistently demonstrate a return on their agentic AI initiatives and lack clear frameworks for assessing whether those initiatives deliver sufficient value to justify continued investment. To address these challenges, financial institutions are implementing disciplined cost and performance controls to continue their innovation drives. Most organizations are deploying or expect to adopt intelligent model routing within a year that direct tasks to the most cost-effective and accurate models.
Cloud is a key execution layer for multi-agent systems
According to the report, financial institutions increasingly recognize cloud as the common execution layer that governs how agents access data, make decisions, and take action. Demand is consolidating around major providers with over half of banks and insurers identifying hyperscalers as their preferred partner to govern multi-agent deployments driven by requirements for regulatory and data residency certifications, security and identity frameworks, and auditability at scale.
This need for cloud environments that can support autonomous operations while meeting regulatory requirements is increasing as AI agents are taking on greater decision-making responsibilities. Three quarters of respondents expect them to become a key part of customer engagement within three years, particularly in account servicing, loan origination and underwriting, and product recommendations.
“In just 12 months, financial institutions have moved beyond experimenting with individual AI agents tackling isolated tasks to deploying multi-agent systems that coordinate actions across entire business lines. Yet adoption alone does not create value,” said Ravi Khokhar, Global Head of Cloud for Financial Services at Capgemini. “Successfully scaling these systems requires infrastructure that drives end-to-end orchestration, effective governance and security by design, and clear link into bottom-line impact. Cloud is now the operational foundation that makes all this possible. The few pulling ahead are not treating cloud as a commodity, but as the foundational pillar of their agentic AI strategy.”
Hybrid sourcing to become the dominant approach
To realize this vision, firms are converging on a hybrid sourcing model for agentic AI capabilities that balances building capabilities in-house for differentiation, buying packaged agentic solutions to accelerate deployment at scale, and working with partners for ecosystem depth. This is expected to become the dominant approach for more than two-thirds of financial institutions within three years.
A small number of financial services firms are operationalizing agentic AI to deliver against the bottom-line
The report identifies a small group of financial institutions, representing just 5% of those surveyed, that have already institutionalized the capabilities required to operate agentic AI at enterprise scale. Their edge over the rest of the industry shows up consistently across three priorities: orchestrating agents across business and technology functions, establishing a trusted cloud foundation for autonomous execution, and ensuring AI investments deliver measurable business outcomes.

title: Experian Boost Update Helps Renters and BNPL Users Benefit From Positive Financial Behaviour at the Click of a Button
summary:
Experian today unveiled an enhanced version of Experian Boost, designed to help people unlock better financial opportunities by giving them greater visibility into the financial information lenders increasingly consider when assessing applications.  
Analysis shows that Boost users could benefit from average APR reductions of up to 22%, with an average saving of £340 per year on interest each year, potentially helping them access cheaper borrowing and products that better reflect their circumstances. For those who do not immediately see access to more offers, Boost provides free personalised guidance within the Experian app to help them improve their financial options over time. 
Millions of people responsibly manage financial commitments such as rent, household bills and everyday spending, yet many have limited understanding of how this information may be viewed as part of a lending decision. While traditional credit information remains an important part of the process, lenders increasingly look beyond a credit report to build a broader picture of an applicant's financial circumstances. Boost will now give people insight in to how a lender may view their everyday spending habits, as part of affordability checks, all at the click of a button.  
By securely connecting their bank account, consumers can now instantly see how everyday financial behaviours, including rent payments, Buy Now Pay Later commitments, household bills and account conduct, may influence their financial profile before applying for products such as loans, credit cards, car finance and mortgages. Users also receive personalised insights explaining what may be helping their financial profile, what may be holding it back and actions they can take to strengthen their eligibility over time. 
Experian Boost will also support millions of UK tenants, allowing them to add their rental payments directly to their credit report for the first time, meaning they could improve their credit score and unlock greater access to credit. 
Edu Castro, Managing Director, Consumer Services UK&I at Experian, said: "We're putting more power into people's hands by giving them greater understanding of the financial behaviours that can influence access to credit. At a time when many households are looking for ways to make their money go further, helping people unlock better financial opportunities has never been more important. 
“The latest Experian Boost update helps positive financial behaviours, such as paying rent and household bills on time, work harder for consumers. For some people, that could mean access to lower borrowing costs and savings of hundreds of pounds each year." 
Experian Boost will begin its roll-out this week, with all consumers able to access the service by the end of November.
